reference.about: The master data sheet (track MP, design handover/design/SSE4-matter-pack-design.md): constants of nature, conventions, reference objects, elements, isotopes, substances and mixtures, each value with its source. A value without "check" is verified against its source; "unverified" means the source is named but the number was not read from it; "authored" is a documented stand-in (docs/fudges.md).

constants.name: ordinary matter today, Omega_b

constants.name: dark matter today, Omega_c
constants.mark_note: The amount is measured through gravity alone (the cosmic background, lensing, clusters); no dark matter particle has been detected. A detection, or a theory of gravity that needed none, would change the picture.

groups.name: Cosmos
groups.about: The measured parameters of the universe. Dark matter and dark energy are marked theoretical: their amounts are measured through gravity, their nature is unknown. Change one and the cosmos chain follows: expansion, growth, the web, halo counts, every galaxy's gas supply.

notes.text: SSE4 takes the particle route: dark matter is an unseen particle that adds mass. It does not offer gravity that changes at low acceleration (MOND and its relatives). The web, the count of haloes and the growth of galaxies are built on dark matter, and no agreed theory of altered gravity replaces all three: colliding clusters show the mass sitting apart from the gas, and the neutron-star merger of 2017 ruled out the whole class of theories where gravity waves and light travel at different speeds.

The standard picture keeps passing new tests: counts of 16,000 galaxy clusters agree with the cosmic background's parameters. Gravity's strength has not changed over time where it can be tested: a neutron-star merger bounds the change in G, and red dwarfs, which would remember a jump in G, rule out the recent 4% and 11% steps proposed to ease the Hubble tension. Those test G changing with time, a different idea from MOND.
Kept as a check: the tight link between ordinary matter and rotation speed in galaxies, which haloes must reproduce.
Energy is conserved for a bound object, not for the expanding universe as a whole, so the sheet's ledgers are mass per co-moving region and energy per bound system.
